recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If the work group wants standard email body text, body templates, or Direct-protocol signaling, handle that as a new issue or extension proposal rather than remaining FHIR-21286 cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-21286 asked the Subscription specification to make email delivery more predictable by clarifying human-readable email bodies, machine-readable FHIR attachments, MIME/content-type negotiation, and possible future body text/template/Direct-protocol extensions. The resolution also mentioned SMS as appropriate.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by e78447afbb9b095050ad9b54c9ecab233717223d, which added email/SMS channel narrative including body/attachment and attach=application/fhir+json/xml MIME examples. Jira later recorded 70355f13b223012ee7f9f70eb5a999219cfe7fb1 as another Subscription documentation update that refined the same area.
additional_context: FHIR-18991 and FHIR-18992 provide earlier SMS/email payload and text/plain background. SMS-specific core channel documentation was later removed by fb3fe3195848fb543677d2135c68a54c6a999a4b with the stated reason that there was not enough feedback, and current Subscription source no longer defines SMS as a core channel. FHIR-23738 later served as the R5 Subscription redesign umbrella and explicitly listed FHIR-21286's email text while flattening Subscription.channel.payload to top-level Subscription.contentType and Subscription.content. The original Zulip thread confirms the connectathon rationale and no Confluence refs were found.
reconciliation: Created an empty audit commit because active current source/subscription/subscription-notes.xml already says email message bodies SHALL be human readable, attachments SHOULD be machine readable, contentType refers to body content, and MIME parameters can request FHIR attachments. structuredefinition-Subscription.xml also permits email-specific text/plain/text/html content types. Reintroducing SMS or adding speculative extensions would go beyond current core scope and later history.
